x: Pineapple is the brand partner. Kickoff call targeted for Mon Sep 21 or Tue Sep 22.
Oleg ran the first experiments and built a custom bot. Next step is building out the individual use cases.

w1-0.d: Seed the branding conversation before we sit down.
x: Send prompts to both Claude and ChatGPT so the exercise starts from questions that push us deeper on the brand rather than a blank page.
Oleg needs the updated list of Second Brain use cases, prioritized. Mark owns getting it to him.
With the prioritized list in hand, Oleg moves from the custom-bot experiment to building out the different use cases.

w1-3.d: Wednesday, Thursday or Friday — Ryan and Brian only.
x: Run our own branding exercise using the Claude and ChatGPT prompts as input. This is the one must-do for the two of us this week.

AWS funding would support building out KOVA privacy, security and safety features. Jack puts the request deck together by the end of next week; AWS should come back inside a week or two; the two-to-three month build starts about a week after that. Being able to tell investors AWS is funding $60–75K and bringing their expertise reads almost like a lead investor.

w1-5.d: Get them up the curve before kickoff.
x: Send the Pineapple team everything we have created around branding and the deck so kickoff does not get spent catching them up.
Brian works the onboarding experience and passes the current state to Mark by Friday. The overview gets shared with Lizzie and Jeff next week.

w1-7.d: Both of us on UI/UX this week.
x: Wireframe the primary product this week and next; finalize end of next week, including the onboarding prototype.

w1-8.d: Book it now so next week runs.
x: Tarek UI/UX session, Lizzie and Jeff all need dates. Dates still TBD as of Monday.
Confirm the Pineapple kickoff call for Sep 21 or 22.

Chuck — the Procter & Gamble and Nabisco operator, angel investing in healthcare. Adviser energy: down the field, looking over our shoulder at how we are positioning. His wisdom may be worth more than his money, and his network is powerful. If he is really into it he will find a way to put money in. It does not have to be Chuck, but somebody like a Chuck.

w1-11.d: Ryan has work to share with Brian.
x: The corporate umbrella website needs to be finalized. The marketing website comes later, once the product is signed on.

Get creative about how we capture what the first 20–50 community members think of the experience: how to make the best use of their time, how to give them value, and how to get value back. First draft this week.

w1-13.d: In the next three or four working days.
x: Ryan and Brian review the budget for this plan — by Tuesday Sep 22 at the latest.
Worth evaluating whether any accelerator would form the right relationships for us, independent of what the program itself teaches.
Tarek should be on a standing weekly cadence with us.
Kickoff with Pineapple on Monday or Tuesday, with our branding work and deck already in their hands.
Lizzie is kicked off. We owe her the Onboarding PDF deck next; she starts her onboarding work once she has it.
Beyond onboarding, talk to Jeff about the early community on both the practitioner/facilitator side and finding early testers. Jeff is a potential advisor too.
Continue the UI/UX work with Tarek before Jenni is engaged.

w2-4.d: So we can answer the questions in the room.
x: Ryan and Brian need strong talking points and high-level answers on privacy, security and the tech stack when they talk to stakeholders.

w2-5.d: Know the flow, not the pixels.
x: Detailed Map of Me work starts this week. Goal is a working prototype of the flow by Oct 2; high-fidelity designs wait until the week of Oct 12.
The primary product wireframe, including the onboarding prototype, is finalized end of this week so Jenni has something stable to polish.

w2-7.d: End of next week, one page.
x: Comes out of the UI/UX work Ryan, Brian and Tarek are doing together.

First goal is reinstating the existing entity as the corporate umbrella by next week. Depending on how intensive the process is we may go with a different corporate umbrella name. Entity type — LLC, C Corp, B Corp — still has to be settled before the raise opens.

w2-10.d: Names and roles, not just names.
x: Who we would want on board as advisors and what role each one plays. People who have been there and done that help us directly, and investors value knowing that kind of thinking is around the table.

w2-11.d: Learned this the hard way before.
x: A lot of advisors sign up and then are too busy to do anything. We eventually got there with the previous venture by asking for money. Decide the ask before the outreach starts.

w2-12.d: Ideal vision-board list first, then who to approach early.
x: Content creators in the space we may want to partner with. Some of them may be advisors with upside in what we are doing.

Facilitators who run retreats and workshops can bring participants in ahead of the retreat, and the product can integrate the experience back into real life afterward. Who else belongs on the list, and who can be approached.
List the AI agents we might need. Where it lands depends on what the list turns out to be.

x: Jack assembles the deck for AWS to request funding. Expect a response inside a week or two.

x: Finalize v1 of the user testing process so the early community work can start against it; it keeps evolving after that.

w2-17.d: Which seats, and what each perspective brings.
x: Beyond Lizzie and Jeff — get clear on who sits in which seat, what perspective each brings, and which perspectives we still need to fill.
Which platforms we want, what the presence looks like, and get them live. LinkedIn is the likely first one.
Schedule dedicated time to talk through go-to-market: the initial core community, and then what growth looks like after them.

w2-20.d: Needs to be in place before the October handoff.
x: Probably part-time, to take the Claude Code build the rest of the way. Either someone we already know or someone through lemon.io.

w2-21.d: Ongoing work, the two of them together.
x: Mark and Tarek build out more of the privacy and security architecture.

MCP layer for the integrations — what that pattern looks like here, fleshed out.

When to lean on existing harnesses (LangChain DeepAgents, AWS Bedrock AgentCore harness) instead of hand-rolling an agent loop. Direction: a general-purpose agent layer that picks its own tools and does web search, not a handmade QA bot.
Interviews and selection so they are onboarded before the October handoff.

w3-10.d: A week or two after the request.

Ryan hands the Claude Code build to the developer to take the rest of the way.

x: Solid on the company name, with the entity set up, before we start investor conversations.
The marketing website is up.
Socials live, LinkedIn included.
With Oleg’s two-week audit running Oct 26 – Nov 6, the first version launches the week of Nov 2. Core community can preview the build before then.
The first pitch. Everything in the 45 days points here.
Outreach begins down the prioritized list, with the deck, data room, docs, name and entity already in place.
What we owe Lizzie after Monday’s kickoff. Her onboarding work starts once it is in her hands.
Jeff has not had his kickoff. Get a date on the calendar; the PDF we made for Lizzie is the walkthrough material.
First pass complete by end of week so it can go to Tarek and Brian on Mon Sep 28, then to Mark on Tue Sep 29.
Second review, with Tarek and Brian’s feedback already folded in. Jenni starts after this.
Connects the bot Oleg built last week to the tools we actually work in. Design doc and use cases follow once this is in.
Take the existing agent and run it on a schedule or trigger. First of the use cases, easy first.
Alignment / philosophy agent: recent meetings, Slack and product work against our tenets.
On-track agent: goals and priorities vs. what we are building; connects to the Notion Kova Plan.
Meeting synthesis agent: tag the bot in Slack for weekly themes and cross-meeting comparisons.
Open-thread research agent: research questions left open in a meeting, come back with a short report.
Linear / follow-up agent: nudge on issues sitting two weeks or more.
Hard tier (safety, conversation QA, app QA, feedback agents) needs live user data and a privacy/safety discussion first — not in this sprint.
Audit starts once the initial build is in. Fixes, improvements and additions land through the week of Nov 2. First version launches when this clears.
Sequence: Ryan first pass → Tarek/Brian/Mark review → Jenni finalizes (2 wks) → Ryan + Claude Code (1 wk) → Oleg audit (2 wks) → launch.

review.title: Priorities + decisions
prompts: What are the three most important outcomes this week?
What decisions must Ryan + Brian make?
What is blocking the critical path?
What are we deliberately not doing?

review.title: Top 3 blockers + next 7 days
prompts: Commit to the next 7 days — three outcomes.

blockers.title: Jeff meeting not scheduled
blockers.needs: Review where onboarding stands and walk him through the onboarding experience PDF. Needs: a date on the calendar this week or next.

blockers.title: Corporate umbrella — process weight unknown
blockers.needs: If incorporating the umbrella is intensive we may go with a different corporate structure. Needs: a call on structure before the attorney is engaged Oct 2.

blockers.title: Jenni engaged part-time from Sep 28
blockers.needs: Production-ready UI/UX by Oct 16 assumes Ryan, Brian and Tarek resolve most of the work first and Jenni polishes. Needs: the wireframe locked Sep 25, no slippage.

decisions.title: Entity type — LLC vs. C Corp vs. B Corp
decisions.desc: The entity has to be set up before the raise opens. Decide the structure, then file. If the process is intensive we may go with a different corporate structure.

decisions.title: Accelerators — worth it for the connections?
decisions.desc: Not for what the program teaches, but for the relationships the right accelerator would form. Evaluate and decide before the raise opens.

decisions.title: Advisors — do we ask them to invest?
decisions.desc: Advisors who sign up without money in often turn out too busy to contribute. Decide the ask — pure advisory, advisory plus a check, or upside for content creators and super nodes — before outreach begins.

decisions.title: Practitioner scope — feedback on our work vs. their own version
decisions.desc: Leaning toward Lizzie and Jeff reacting to what we are building rather than producing their own onboarding experience. We have more context on what we are building than they will; the invitation is into our open questions. Compresses their ask from two weeks each to about one.

decisions.title: Fundraising attorney — which of the two we engage
decisions.desc: Both attorneys under consideration have been spoken to. Decide and engage for the fundraising docs.

decisions.title: Map of Me reveal — full reveal vs. progressive reveal
decisions.desc: The Oct 2 prototype should establish the flow and what we serve up. High-fidelity designs follow the week of Oct 12.

decisions.title: Name — new name vs. KOVA-for-now
decisions.desc: Pineapple should reach a name or finalists before the first pitch. If it is not settled, pitch as KOVA and treat the name as in progress.

decisions.title: Second Brain — first proactive workflow
decisions.desc: One workflow, chosen off what the prioritized use cases actually surface. Not eight agents.
